NAME: Intangible Cash Conversion Share
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(oancf, ADD(ABS(oibdp), ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)))), 1)), IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), ADD(ABS(oibdp), ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)))), 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: Firms with high cash conversion of their operating surplus and a meaningful share of that surplus reinvested into R&D and advertising earn higher future returns.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: This tests whether intangible reinvestment is supported by cash realization rather than simply pairing cash profitability with raw R&D intensity. The reinvestment-share denominator is the current operating-surplus-plus-intangibles pool, so it focuses on validated internal funding capacity rather than size-scaled spending alone.
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: Intangible SG&A Operating Leverage
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(WINSOR(TREND(RATIO(oibdp, xsga), 3), 1)), IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(TS_SUM(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), 3), TS_SUM(xsga, 3)), 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: Firms whose SG&A is heavily intangible-investment-oriented and whose operating profit per SG&A dollar is improving earn higher future returns.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: This is a dynamic version of validated intangible overhead productivity: it asks whether an intangible-heavy SG&A base is becoming more productive over time. Smoothing the SG&A and intangible-spend base reduces single-period denominator noise while preserving the economic interaction.
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: Intangible-Adjusted Margin High
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(TS_RANK(RATIO(ADD(oibdp, ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0))), sale), 5)), IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), sale), 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: Intangible-intensive firms whose intangible-adjusted operating margins are near their own historical highs earn higher future returns.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Adding back R&D and advertising measures economic profitability before expensed intangible investment, while the time-series rank asks whether that productivity is unusually strong for the firm. The current intangible-intensity leg ensures the signal is not just an own-history profitability rank among firms with little intangible investment.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 4---
NAME: Goodwill Cash Recovery
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(WINSOR(TREND(RATIO(oancf, sale), 3), 1)), IND_RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(gdwl, 0), ADD(at, COALESCE(gdwl, 0)))))
HYPOTHESIS: Goodwill-heavy firms with improving cash margins earn higher future returns because acquired intangible assets are being economically validated.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Prior goodwill-decay signals indicate that deteriorating profitability among goodwill-heavy firms is costly; this tests the opposite recovery channel using cash rather than accrual margins. The interaction avoids treating goodwill as uniformly bad by requiring evidence that acquired intangibles are producing improving cash profitability.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 5---
NAME: Expensed Intangible Recognition Gap
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(oibdp, sale), 1)), IND_RANK(WINSOR(SUB(RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), sale), RATIO(DELTA(COALESCE(SUB(intan, COALESCE(gdwl, 0)), 0), 1), sale)), 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: Profitable firms whose internal intangible investment is expensed rather than recognized as balance-sheet intangible asset growth earn higher future returns.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The second leg compares two flow-scaled quantities: current expensed R&D/advertising intensity versus the change in identifiable non-goodwill intangible assets. High values identify profitable firms where accounting is most likely understating internally generated productive capital.
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel

---SIGNAL 6---
NAME: Maturing Intangible Cash Dropthrough
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(LAG(RATIO(TS_SUM(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), 3), at), 1)), MUL(IND_RANK(WINSOR(TREND(RATIO(oancf, ADD(ABS(oibdp), ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)))), 3), 1)), IND_RANK(WINSOR(NEG(TREND(RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), sale), 3)), 1))))
HYPOTHESIS: Firms with prior intangible investment, improving cash conversion, and declining current intangible-spend intensity are entering a profitable harvest phase.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: This distinguishes intangible productivity from perpetual spending by requiring lagged investment and subsequent cash drop-through as current spending intensity eases. The mechanism is a maturation test: prior intangible capital should begin generating cash without needing the same level of ongoing expense.
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel

---CRITIQUE Intangible Cash Conversion Share---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: This is a near-mechanical restatement of the already-tested "Self-Funded Intangible Reinvestment" (identical reinvestment-share leg up to the ABS denominator, and a first leg that differs only by adding back the intangible spend already captured in leg two), which failed with fmb 1.38 and negative alpha, so it offers no new economic content.

---CRITIQUE Intangible SG&A Operating Leverage---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: The intangible-share-of-SG&A leg is essentially the archived "Productive Intangible Overhead" second leg with 3-year smoothing, and swapping the level of oibdp/xsga for its 3-year trend recreates the margin-trend × intangible-intensity structure already tested in "Intangible Harvest Operating Leverage," making this a hybrid variant of two weak-to-moderate predecessors rather than a new mechanism.

---CRITIQUE Intangible-Adjusted Margin High---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: The two legs are mechanically coupled — adding xrd+xad back into the margin numerator means a firm whose intangible intensity is rising automatically ranks high in its own time-series of "intangible-adjusted margin" — so the interaction can fire on spending escalation rather than productivity, and the design otherwise overlaps "Sustained Intangible Margin Breakout" (fmb 1.63, alpha 0.003) and the TS_RANK construction of "Goodwill-Light Intangible Cash High."

---CRITIQUE Goodwill Cash Recovery---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: This is the mirror image of the already-evaluated "Acquired Intangible Cash Decay" (goodwill weight × cash-margin trend, sign flipped) and therefore mostly re-tests the same axis, and the denominator ADD(at, gdwl) double-counts goodwill since it is already inside total assets.

---CRITIQUE Expensed Intangible Recognition Gap---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: The expensed-versus-recognized intangible "gap" leg is a genuinely new comparison in this archive and a coherent test of accounting understatement, though the reviewer should note two risks: for firms with missing intan the leg degenerates to plain R&D/advertising intensity (already paired with margins in several archived signals), and high values can be driven mechanically by amortization-driven declines in intangible assets rather than by internal capital formation.

---CRITIQUE Maturing Intangible Cash Dropthrough---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: Two of the three legs (lagged intangible intensity, negative trend in intangible spend intensity) are identical to "Intangible Harvest Operating Leverage," so the only change is substituting a cash-conversion trend for the margin trend — a cosmetic variant — and the ABS(oibdp) denominator makes the conversion ratio non-monotonic for loss-making firms.

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: Intangible Overhead Discipline
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(oibdp, sale), 1)), MUL(IND_RANK(WINSOR(MA(RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), sale), 3), 1)), IND_RANK(WINSOR(NEG(TREND(RATIO(SUB(xsga, ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0))), sale), 3)), 1))))

REASONING: This avoids reusing the intangible-share-of-SG&A leg by explicitly separating intangible spending from residual SG&A overhead. The mechanism is overhead discipline: R&D and advertising are more credible when administrative or maintenance SG&A is being scaled down while operating margins remain positive.

NAME: Profitability Outruns Intangible Spend
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), 5), at)), IND_RANK(WINSOR(SUB(TS_RANK(RATIO(oibdp, sale), 5), TS_RANK(RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), sale), 5)), 1)))

The relative time-series spread penalizes cases where the apparent profitability signal is merely synchronized with rising intangible expense intensity.

NAME: Acquisition Platform Internal Innovation
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(oibdp, sale), 1)), MUL(IND_RANK(WINSOR(TREND(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), revt), 3), 1)), IND_RANK(WINSOR(MUL(RATIO(COALESCE(gdwl, 0), at), MA(RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), sale), 3)), 1))))

EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional
REASONING: This is not the mirror image of goodwill cash decay; it tests whether acquired platforms are being productively enhanced with internal R&D and advertising. Gross-margin improvement provides a product or pricing-power validation channel, while operating margin ensures the improvement reaches profitability.

---SIGNAL 5---
NAME: Intangible Demand Resilience
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(oibdp, sale), 1)), MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), 5), at)), IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(sale, TS_MAX(sale, 5)), 1))))
HYPOTHESIS: Intangible-intensive firms with current profitability and sales near their own historical peak earn higher future returns.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel
REASONING: This replaces the harvest-phase duplicate with a demand-resilience mechanism rather than using lagged intensity and falling spend intensity again.
